answer: Submissions that land within 265 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The trellis detector writes to juniper, and thread shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, and therefore the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 87 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 23 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
